title: Virtual power plant capacity expands 25.9% year-over-year to reach 47.2 GW, according to Wood Mackenzie
gist: Wood Mackenzie's 2026 North America VPP report finds behind-the-meter flexible capacity grew 25.9% YoY to 47.2 GW, deepening faster than it broadened, as escalating turbine costs make distributed BESS VPPs cost-competitive per kW. Residential wholesale VPP capacity jumped 155%, a new 1 GW VPP pipeline targets data center load, and revenue accounting plus enrollment models (opt-out vs opt-in) are becoming the key competitive variables.

themes.theme: VPP capacity growth and market deepening

insights.claim: North American virtual power plant (VPP) behind-the-meter flexible capacity grew 25.9% year-over-year to reach 47.2 GW in 2026, per Wood Mackenzie.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Flexible distributed capacity is scaling at ~26%/yr, a growing addressable market for aggregators, DER software and residential storage providers.

insights.claim: The VPP market deepened more than it broadened in 2026: capacity grew 25.9% while the number of company deployments, unique offtakers and monetized market/utility programs each grew less than 15%.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Growth is concentrating in existing programs and players, favoring incumbents with scale over new entrants.
insights.locator: The report, “2026 North America virtual power plant

insights.claim: Storage and EV penetration relative to thermostats in VPPs grew 19.7% year-over-year, outpacing 2025's growth rate.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: VPP mix is shifting from thermostat demand response toward batteries and EVs, which offer higher-value dispatchable capacity.
insights.locator: Storage and EV penetration relative to thermostats

insights.claim: Economic participants were the only VPP segment to contract, shrinking 13.5% year-over-year.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Economic (price-responsive) demand response is losing share; watch whether capacity-based programs fully displace it.
insights.locator: Storage and EV penetration relative to thermostats

insights.claim: Escalating turbine costs, affordability concerns and slow supply response to large loads are driving increased interest in virtual power plants.
insights.speaker: Elham Akhavan
insights.so_what: Gas turbine supply bottlenecks are a tailwind for distributed flexibility as an alternative capacity resource.
insights.quote: Escalating turbine costs, affordability concerns and slow supply response to large loads are driving more interest in VPPs

insights.claim: With heavy-turbine capex up more than 80% since 2020, battery energy storage (BESS) VPPs now win on cost per kW in 2026, and distributed BESS remains the most cost-effective option in this time frame.
insights.speaker: Elham Akhavan
insights.so_what: If turbine capex inflation persists, utilities and capacity buyers may increasingly procure distributed BESS VPPs instead of new peakers; relevant to turbine OEMs and storage developers.
insights.quote: with heavy-turbine capex expanding more than 80% since 2020, BESS VPPs now win on cost per kW in 2026
insights.locator: Akhavan noted that with heavy-turbine capex

insights.claim: Residential VPP capacity in wholesale markets grew 155% year-over-year, the largest jump of any segment.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Residential batteries are becoming a material wholesale-market resource; positive for residential storage installers and retail-energy aggregators.
insights.locator: The largest jump in VPP wholesale market

insights.claim: Residential's share of wholesale-market VPP capacity more than doubled, driven by opt-out enrollment and retailer-led battery growth.
insights.speaker: Max Issokson
insights.so_what: Retailers bundling batteries and default (opt-out) enrollment are the playbook for scaling residential VPPs quickly.
insights.quote: Residential’s share of wholesale-market VPP capacity more than doubled, reflecting opt-out enrollment and retailer-led battery growth

insights.claim: Deployed storage does not automatically translate into VPP capacity: opt-out enrollment can shift capacity overnight, while opt-in models and data access barriers continue to constrain growth.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Track program enrollment design and data-access rules, not just installed battery counts, when forecasting VPP capacity.
insights.quote: deployed storage does not automatically translate into VPP capacity
insights.locator: At the same time, the report cautions

insights.claim: PJM and ERCOT, the regions with the greatest utility commitments to data center capacity, also have the greatest disclosed VPP offtake capacity.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Data-center-driven load growth and VPP demand are co-located; PJM and ERCOT are the key markets to watch for VPP monetization.
insights.locator: PJM and ERCOT remain the regions

insights.claim: MISO summer capacity prices rose from $30 to $384-424/MW-day in 2026, but aggregation rules still limit VPP growth there.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: MISO has strong price signals for VPPs; a change in aggregation rules could unlock rapid capacity additions.
insights.quote: Summer capacity prices rose significantly in MISO this year, from $30 to $384-424/MW-day, but aggregation rules still limit growth.
insights.locator: Summer capacity prices rose significantly in MISO

insights.claim: Arizona, Virginia and Illinois are building new VPP programs that may increase capacity, signalling emerging growth markets beyond traditional leaders.
insights.speaker: Elham Akhavan
insights.so_what: New state programs are potential growth catalysts for VPP aggregators expanding footprints.
insights.quote: Arizona, Virginia and Illinois are building new programs that may increase capacity

insights.claim: California, historically a strong VPP market, will see its future growth depend on SB 913 versus one-off DSGS funding.
insights.speaker: Elham Akhavan
insights.so_what: Watch passage/implementation of SB 913 as a binary driver of durable California VPP funding.
insights.quote: its future growth depends on SB 913 versus one-off DSGS funding

insights.claim: VPP providers disclosed a 1 GW pipeline of capacity specifically targeting data center load in 2026, a category absent from the prior year's scorecard.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: VPPs are emerging as a direct response to AI/data-center infrastructure demand, opening a new offtaker class for aggregators.
insights.quote: a 1 GW pipeline of capacity specifically targeting data center load
insights.locator: The 2026 report identifies a new signal

insights.claim: Competition among commercial and industrial VPP aggregators is tightening, with battery ownership and optimization emerging as key differentiators.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: C&I aggregators that own and optimize batteries may capture more value than asset-light players.
insights.locator: Competition among commercial and industrial aggregators

insights.claim: Financiers are divided on accounting for VPP revenue—some price it directly into storage leases while others pass it to customers as bill credits or incentives—and that treatment is becoming a defining competitive variable.
insights.speaker: Elham Akhavan
insights.so_what: Financing structures that monetize VPP revenue upfront in leases could lower customer cost and win share in residential/C&I storage.
insights.quote: How that revenue is treated is becoming a defining competitive variable.
